# Purpose

`inspect_sales.R` reads a fictional coffee-sales file into R and displays its structure and first rows. The purpose is to make an import workflow understandable and reproducible. This example does not analyse business performance or calculate financial measures.

# Inputs

The script reads `data/synthetic_sales.csv`, relative to the repository root. The input has a header and four columns: `sale_date`, `product`, `units` and `unit_price_cad`. All records are synthetic. Dates stay as character values at import; quantities and prices are intended to import as numeric fields.

# Requirements

Base R is sufficient to run the script. Rendering this document additionally needs `rmarkdown`, `knitr` and Pandoc. RStudio normally supplies Pandoc. Run the render command from the repository root so that the relative paths resolve correctly.

# Script walkthrough

## Import the data

The following highlighted example explains the import line. It is displayed without execution to avoid duplicating the executable chunk below.

```{r import-example, eval=FALSE}
sales <- read.csv("data/synthetic_sales.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
```

`read.csv()` reads the local file. `stringsAsFactors = FALSE` keeps text as character values. The assignment places the imported table in `sales`.

## Inspect the imported object

```{r inspection-example, eval=FALSE}
str(sales)
head(sales)
```

`str()` displays the object structure and column types. `head()` displays the beginning of the table. These views help a reader notice obvious import problems, but they do not establish that every value is valid.

## Run the single documented script

This named executable chunk sources the supplied script once. When knitted in RStudio, its console output will appear beneath the chunk. No output is invented in the source document.

```{r run-inspection, echo=TRUE}
source("inspect_sales.R", local = knitr::knit_global())
```

# Outputs

## Expected console display

The display should identify `sales` as a data frame and show its four columns. Text fields should remain character values, `units` should import as an integer and `unit_price_cad` as numeric with the supplied CSV. `head()` should show the supplied records. These expectations are not substituted for an actual R run.

## Files and objects

The script creates `sales` in the knitting environment and prints its structure and first rows. It writes no output files. Knitting this document creates `Sales_Documentation.html` separately through the R Markdown rendering process.
